Companion Animal Travel Desk Travel Welfare Guidance

This section explains how staff support safe, calm travel for companion animals and their travelers.

The Companion Animal Travel Desk must give clear, respectful instructions before boarding, during any transfer, and after arrival. Staff should confirm that carriers are secure, labels are readable, and animal welfare checks are completed without delay. When a traveler seems worried, the senior coordinator should listen carefully, speak plainly, and record the concern in the service log. If a claim for escape in transit is raised, <<FACT F120>> the staff member should continue with the welfare review and advise the traveler on the next step. In all cases, the crew must keep communication steady and courteous, and must not promise an outcome that has not been approved.

If a cabin overheating incident is reported, <<FACT F111>> the coordinator must arrange immediate support, note the condition of the animal, and follow the incident pathway with care. Supervisors should remind staff that prompt action protects trust and helps reduce further distress. For guidance on any unresolved case, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
